Y94.tagline: The Eagles beat the Colts 48-10 in Super Bowl CLIII for a fourth straight title, the Cowboys end a 49-game winning streak, and Ryland Maxwell catches a record 53 touchdown passes on his way to a first MVP.

articles.headline: Four in a Row, and Maxwell Runs the Gauntlet: Eagles Rout the Colts 48-10
articles.dek: Philadelphia went 15-2, saw a 49-game winning streak end in Dallas, then won Super Bowl CLIII at home. Ryland Maxwell's first MVP completed a full set of offensive awards.
body: Dorren Skura's Eagles are champions for the fourth season running. Philadelphia beat the Colts 48-10 in Super Bowl CLIII, the 153rd edition of the game, at home, two seasons after beating the same club 30-21 in Super Bowl CLI. The 38-point margin was the widest of the Eagles' season.

The streak is over, though. Philadelphia had not lost since week 5 of Y92 when it went to Dallas in week 16 and fell 35-32, ending a run of 49 straight wins by Skura's club with two Super Bowls inside it. The Cowboys won again in Philadelphia two weeks later, 26-24. Those were the only defeats of the year.

Otherwise the standard held. The Eagles allowed 402 points, the fewest in the league, scored 602, behind only Pittsburgh's 628, and finished first in the power rankings with a point differential of 200. They went 8-1 on the road and 9-2 against clubs with winning records.

The playoffs belonged to them. The Lions fell 48-26 in the divisional round and the Packers 32-19 in the conference final. Then Indianapolis arrived with a 13-4 record and the league's leading rusher, River Kuechly, and scored only 10.

The biggest individual story belonged to Ryland Maxwell, "Mad Max". He caught 53 touchdown passes, a record, and was named Most Valuable Player for the first time. That made him the first player on file to win every award an offensive player can win: 11 rings, 3 Offensive Player of the Year awards, 5 Super Bowl MVPs and an Offensive Rookie of the Year award to go with the MVP. Call it running the Gauntlet. Bones Crawford, "The Doctor", was Super Bowl MVP for the 2nd time after throwing 68 touchdown passes.

articles.headline: Mad Max Catches 53 Touchdown Passes, Wins His First MVP and Completes the Gauntlet
articles.dek: Ryland Maxwell ran for 1,692 yards and caught 71 passes in 19 games, 53 of them for touchdowns, and passed God Johnson on the Career Legacy list.
body: For years Ryland Maxwell has been the league's most feared runner. In Y94 he became its most dangerous receiver as well. Maxwell caught 71 passes for only 391 yards, 5.5 a catch, and 53 of them went for touchdowns. That broke the season mark on Skura's record board, which God Johnson had held since Y63.

He still ran the ball. Maxwell added 1,692 rushing yards and 11 rushing touchdowns, and injury cost him 1 of Philadelphia's 20 games. The league named him Most Valuable Player for the first time in his career, ahead of his own quarterback and his 68 touchdown passes. It was the one major award an offensive player can win that he had never won; no player on file had collected all of them before.

His career rushing total reached 27,393 yards, 2,886 more than Lane McCoy, and his 366 rushing touchdowns top Skura's record board. His Career Legacy rose from 11,965 to 13,107, past God Johnson's 12,655, and only Sherman Brandson, at 13,488, rates higher. He has 11 rings, every one won with Skura, and his card is now worth 39,532.

articles.headline: The Doctor Throws 68 Touchdown Passes and Is Super Bowl MVP Again
articles.dek: Bones Crawford threw for 5,131 yards and won his sixth ring. He also threw 20 interceptions, the most in the league.
body: Bones Crawford played all 20 of Philadelphia's games for the second straight season and threw 68 touchdown passes, 4 more than in his MVP season a year earlier. He threw for 5,131 yards and ran for 14 more scores, and his 3.4 touchdown passes a game led the league by a distance: Solomon Toohill of the Packers was next with 44.

There was a cost. Crawford threw 20 interceptions, more than twice as many as any other passer; Lukas Samuels of the Cardinals was next with 8. It did not matter in the Super Bowl, where Crawford was named MVP for the 2nd time as the Eagles scored 48.

Most of the touchdowns had one destination. Of his 68 scoring passes, 53 went to Ryland Maxwell and 15 to everyone else. Crawford's overall rose from 86 to 91, his Career Legacy from 8,158 to 8,987, and his card's value by 162%. He has 6 rings, every one won with the Eagles.

articles.headline: Dallas Ends the Streak at 49, Then Beats the Eagles Again
articles.dek: The Cowboys won 35-32 at home in week 16 and 26-24 in Philadelphia in week 18. The Giants lost twice more.
body: The Cowboys had not been much of a problem. In the six seasons since Skura arrived in Philadelphia they had beaten his Eagles once. Then Dallas did it twice in three weeks. In week 16 the Cowboys won 35-32 at home and ended a winning streak that had run since early in Y92: 49 straight wins, two Super Bowls inside it. In week 18 they came to Philadelphia and won 26-24, the only home defeat of the Eagles' season.

Dallas finished only 9-8, against the hardest schedule in the league by strength of schedule, and still beat the champions twice. Lewis Pettis led the league with 6 interceptions, and Taco Coulter caught 14 touchdown passes, more than any other receiver.

The Giants could not do the same. Philadelphia won 24-17 in New York in week 8 and 46-27 at home in week 15. Ty Lock, who played his 300th game this season, threw 22 touchdown passes for a 9-8 club, and New York still had not beaten the Eagles since Y88.

articles.headline: Viennes Repeats as Offensive Player of the Year, With Wingo 47 Yards Behind
articles.dek: Keenan Viennes caught 99 passes for 2,041 yards and Calvin Wingo II 98 for 1,994. Nobody else in the league came close.
body: For the second year running the league's two most productive receivers wore the same uniform. Keenan Viennes caught 99 passes for 2,041 yards in 20 games and was named Offensive Player of the Year for the 2nd time. Calvin Wingo II caught 98 for 1,994. The next receiver on the list, Taco Coulter of the Cowboys, had 1,036.

What neither of them did much of was score. With Ryland Maxwell catching 53 touchdown passes out of the backfield, Viennes finished with 8 touchdown catches and Wingo with 7, down from 29 and 19 a year earlier.
The market did not mind. Wingo's overall rose from 86 to 91 and his card's value by 163.6%. Viennes went from 73 to 79, and his card, priced at 49 a year ago, now sells for 160.

articles.headline: Akiem Brock Makes 75 Blocks, Twice as Many as Anyone Else
articles.dek: The Eagles lineman's card tripled in value. Snoop Dotson and Jacob Proise rose with him.
body: Every Eagles touchdown started somewhere, and in Y94 it usually started with Akiem Brock. The lineman made 75 blocks in 20 games; Cethan Qualls of the Ravens was second in the league with 37. Brock's overall rose from 94 to 98, his Career Legacy passed 10,000, and his card's value rose 201.5% to 25,260.

Snoop Dotson had 3 sacks, tied for the most in the league, with 81 tackles, 2 interceptions and a forced fumble, and his overall climbed from 88 to 93. Tight end Jacob Proise caught 42 passes for 760 yards, and his card rose 256.2%, the biggest gain among the market's established cards. In the secondary Quincy Booker intercepted 4 passes and Koa Zuber, "Uber Feasts", made 144 tackles.

articles.headline: The Colts Reach a Second Super Bowl in Three Years and Lose to Philadelphia Again
articles.dek: Indianapolis went 13-4 behind River Kuechly's 1,825 rushing yards and 35 touchdowns, then scored 10 in the final.
body: Indianapolis has now met Skura's Eagles in two of the last three Super Bowls and lost both, 30-21 in Y92 and 48-10 in Y94. The first time, Dwayne Skura was on the Colts' sideline, a season after winning a ring in Philadelphia. This time he had retired, and the Colts arrived with a new core.

River Kuechly led the league with 1,825 rushing yards and 35 rushing touchdowns in 21 games, and caught just 1 pass. Korey Friend threw for 4,420 yards and 36 touchdowns with 3 interceptions. Reggie Deayon, a rookie defensive back, made 228 tackles and intercepted 5 passes, tied for the second most in the league.

The Colts finished 13-4 and fourth in the power rankings. Kuechly's overall climbed from 71 to 72 and his card still sells for 49. They have the pieces. They do not yet have an answer for Philadelphia.

articles.headline: Atwell Closes to 126 Tackles of the Record, and Spector Passes 400
articles.dek: Kyron Atwell is chasing K'Lavon Settle's 3,185. Siran Spector moved to fourth on the career rushing touchdowns list. Odell Hainsey retired 2 interceptions short.
body: Kyron Atwell made 206 tackles for the Jets in 17 games and reached 3,059 for his career. Only two players have more: Terron Stidham with 3,132 and K'Lavon Settle, whose 3,185 are the league record. Atwell is 73 behind Stidham and 126 behind Settle, one ordinary season away from both.

Siran Spector ran for 29 touchdowns for the Texans and finished the season with 402, past 400 and past Trequan Jensen and Rondale Ikarras. Ahead of him now are Danny Diggs with 408, Tim Wright with 417 and Lane McCoy's record 458.

Two chases stalled. Odell Hainsey retired after Y93 with 41 interceptions, 2 short of Damar Hobbs's record 43, and 2,989 tackles. Deshone Bello of the Jets did not record a sack in 17 games and stays at 23, 1 behind Kalif Suh.

articles.headline: Lazard's Touchdowns Fall From 39 to 18, and Cincinnati Falls to 6-11
articles.dek: Alshon Lazard played every game again, but the Bengals dropped from second in the power rankings to 27th.
body: A year ago Alshon Lazard threw 39 touchdown passes as a rookie and the Bengals went 14-3. In his second season he played all 17 games and threw for 3,203 yards with only 3 interceptions, but he finished with 18 touchdown passes. Cincinnati went 6-11 and allowed 594 points.

The ratings moved with the results. The market's skill score for Lazard fell from 91 to 84, his overall rose only from 63 to 64, and his card slipped from 16 to 15. Grover Calitro ran for 1,569 yards for the Bengals, but Cincinnati scored just 435 points, among the fewest in the league.
A Rookie of the Year season is not a promise. Lazard still has time to become the quarterback his first year suggested. After Y94, he no longer has the benefit of the doubt.

articles.headline: Fox, Hainsey and Dwayne Skura Lead a Long Retirement List
articles.dek: Tevin Fox leaves with 69,973 passing yards and no ring. Dwayne Skura leaves with 4 rings and a Defensive Player of the Year award.
body: Tevin Fox played 403 games, threw for 69,973 yards and 618 touchdowns, and never won a ring. He went through his final season, Y93, without throwing an interception. Odell Hainsey retired with 2,989 tackles and 41 interceptions, the third most on file.

Dwayne Skura won 4 rings and was Defensive Player of the Year in his first season after Philadelphia traded him to the Colts. He retires with 1,595 tackles and 21 interceptions. Trequan Roberts, who spent Y93 with the 3-14 Saints, leaves with 3 rings and 1,949 tackles.

The defensive side lost the most. Oli Alaka retires with 2,851 tackles and 38 interceptions, Linval Laulile, a former Defensive Player of the Year, with 2,765 tackles, and defensive lineman Dallin Santoso with 1,355 tackles and 12 sacks.

articles.headline: Quick Hits
articles.dek: Around the league in Y94.
body: Abraham Jack of the 13-4 Bills was Defensive Player of the Year with 211 tackles and 3 interceptions. DQ Watts of the Texans made 255, the most in the league.
The 2-15 Titans beat the 10-6-1 Ravens 42-26 in week 5, the upset of the season, and went 0-8 on the road while allowing 657 points.
The Patriots beat the Broncos 68-23 in week 3, and the Dolphins won 61-50 at Carolina in week 9, 111 points in all.
The Chiefs tied twice, 40-40 at Miami and 41-41 at Baltimore, and finished 9-6-2.
The Steelers scored 628 points, the most in the league, and went 13-4.
Kaulani Rahman caught 43 passes for 268 yards in 17 games for the 8-9 Rams.
Rookie quarterback Olivier Slade threw 25 touchdown passes and 4 interceptions for the 4-12-1 Panthers.

Y95.tagline: The Eagles go 17-0 again and edge the Chiefs 24-19 in Super Bowl CLIV for a fifth straight title, Ryland Maxwell runs the career rushing record out to 29,534 yards, and Dallas falls from streak breakers to 2-15.

articles.headline: Perfect Again: Eagles Go 17-0 and Hold Off the Chiefs 24-19 in Super Bowl CLIV
articles.dek: Philadelphia won all 20 of its games, had the league's best offense and its best defense, and needed every point of a 5-point Super Bowl margin for a fifth straight title.
body: Dorren Skura's Eagles have done it again. Two seasons after going 17-0 in Y93, Philadelphia went 17-0 once more, swept three playoff games and beat the Chiefs 24-19 in Super Bowl CLIV, the 154th edition of the game. It is the club's fifth straight championship and the 13th season in which one of his clubs went unbeaten.

For most of the year nobody came close. The Eagles scored 624 points, the most in the league, and allowed 326, the fewest, for a point differential of 298. They went 8-0 at home, 9-0 on the road and 7-0 against clubs with winning records. The widest margin was 48-6 over the Jaguars in week 9. The narrowest came in week 12 in New York, 32-31 over the Giants.

The playoffs were quick work until the last game. Tampa Bay fell 40-10 in the divisional round and Detroit 30-16 in the conference final. Then came Kansas City, 15-2 and second in the power rankings. The Chiefs held Philadelphia to 24 points, matching its lowest total of the season, and lost by 5, the closest Super Bowl of the five-title run.

The usual names carried the trophy. Ryland Maxwell, "Mad Max", was Super Bowl MVP for the 6th time, the most on file, in a season in which he missed 2 games through injury and still led the league in rushing. Bones Crawford, "The Doctor", was named Most Valuable Player for the 5th time. Calvin Wingo II was Offensive Player of the Year. Maxwell's ring was his 12th; Crawford and Akiem Brock each won their 7th.

articles.headline: Mad Max Puts the Career Rushing Record Out of Sight
articles.dek: Ryland Maxwell ran for 2,141 yards and 30 touchdowns, reached 29,534 career yards and passed Sherman Brandson at the top of the Career Legacy list.
body: Ryland Maxwell took the career rushing record from Lane McCoy two seasons ago. In Y95 he made it his own. Maxwell ran for 2,141 yards, the most in the league by 386 over Maurice Vigil of the Chiefs, and scored 30 rushing touchdowns. Injury cost him 2 of Philadelphia's 20 games. He finished the season at 29,534 career yards, 5,027 clear of McCoy's 24,507.

His 396 rushing touchdowns top Skura's record board, but the league mark is another matter: McCoy scored 458, 62 more. The receiving line came back to earth after his 53-touchdown season. Maxwell caught 19 passes, and 7 of them went for scores.

Everything else kept growing. His 12th ring is the most on file, and every one came with Skura. His 6th Super Bowl MVP is also the most on file. His Career Legacy rose from 13,107 to 14,019, past Brandson's 13,540, and no player on file now rates higher. His card is worth 44,400. He is 33, and the next chase is the one he cannot run down on the field: time.

articles.headline: The Doctor Wins a 5th MVP, and Akiem Brock Blocks His Way to a 7th Ring
articles.dek: Bones Crawford threw 52 touchdown passes in 18 games. Akiem Brock made 57 blocks, 19 more than any other lineman.
body: Bones Crawford's numbers came down from his 68-touchdown season, and he won the league's top award anyway. Crawford threw for 4,271 yards and 52 touchdowns, the most in the league by 12, and ran for 6 more. Injury cost him 2 of Philadelphia's 20 games. He was named Most Valuable Player for the 5th time, level with Wayne Wilson and Ray Waller and behind only Michael Wilson's 6 and Sherman Brandson's 8.

There is a flaw in the case, and it is the same one as last year. Crawford threw 10 interceptions, the most in the league, a season after leading it with 20. Nobody seemed to mind. His overall rose from 91 to 94 and his card's value by 48.6%.

In front of him, Akiem Brock made 57 blocks in 20 games. Shaquem Goedert of the Chiefs was next with 38. Brock and Crawford both won their 7th ring, every one of them in Philadelphia, and Brock's card is now worth 27,222.

articles.headline: Wingo Takes Over in Philadelphia, and Viennes Finds New York Harder
articles.dek: Calvin Wingo II caught 114 passes for 2,267 yards and 25 touchdowns and was Offensive Player of the Year. Keenan Viennes, the winner a year ago, managed 726 yards for the 5-11-1 Jets.
body: A year ago Calvin Wingo II finished 47 yards behind Keenan Viennes and watched his teammate collect a second Offensive Player of the Year award. In Y95 Viennes was playing for the Jets, and Wingo had the field to himself. He caught 114 passes for 2,267 yards and 25 touchdowns in 20 games, up from 1,994 yards and 7 scores, and was named Offensive Player of the Year for the 2nd time. His card's value rose from 1,758 to 2,584.
Philadelphia barely noticed the change. Rookie Payton Jarrett caught 81 passes for 1,450 yards and 15 touchdowns.

New York was a harder place. Viennes played all 17 of the Jets' games and caught 82 passes for 726 yards, 8.9 a catch after 20.6 a year earlier. The Jets finished 5-11-1, and in week 13 the Eagles beat them 35-19. The ratings held up, his overall rising from 79 to 82, but the production did not. In Philadelphia he was a deep threat in the best offense in the league. In New York he has been a possession receiver on a losing club.

articles.headline: From Streak Breakers to 2-15: Dallas Falls Apart
articles.dek: The Cowboys beat the champions twice in Y94. A year later they lost every home game and finished last in the power rankings.
body: No club fell further. A year after the Cowboys ended Philadelphia's 49-game winning streak and beat the champions twice, Dallas finished 2-15, the worst record in the league. The Cowboys went 0-8 at home, allowed 617 points and finished 32nd in the power rankings with a point differential of minus 200. They had gone 9-8 in Y94.
The Eagles took both meetings this time, 32-27 in Dallas in week 3 and 40-22 in Philadelphia on the final weekend. Dallas won only at Jacksonville and, in week 15, 20-13 at the Giants.

It was not for lack of a star. Lewis Pettis intercepted 5 passes, tied for the most in the league, and his overall rose from 92 to 95. The passing game around him faded: Taco Coulter, who caught 14 touchdown passes a year ago, caught 5. The schedule was tough, with a strength of 0.564, but the Jets faced a tougher one and won 5 games. Dallas had no such excuse.

articles.headline: The Chiefs Go 15-2 and Come Within 5 Points
articles.dek: Kansas City reached its first Super Bowl since Y79 behind Roc Dunkle's 40 touchdown passes and Maurice Vigil's league-leading 34 rushing scores.
body: Kansas City was the second-best team in the league all season, and for one night it came close to being the best. The Chiefs went 9-6-2 in Y94. In Y95 they went 15-2, 8-1 at home and 7-1 on the road, and won 8 straight at one point. Their only defeats came 16-9 at Arizona in week 2 and 29-21 at home to the 6-11 Raiders in week 12, the upset of the season.

Roc Dunkle threw for 4,216 yards and 40 touchdowns, tied for second in the league, with 6 interceptions. Maurice Vigil, 34, led the league with 34 rushing touchdowns, ran for 1,755 yards and passed 20,000 career yards and 350 career rushing touchdowns along the way. Shaquem Goedert's 38 blocks were second only to Akiem Brock's.

It was the Chiefs' first Super Bowl since a 44-6 loss to the Packers in Y79, and they kept it close, losing 24-19. The problem is the opponent. Kansas City has now met Skura's Eagles 5 times since Y88 and lost all 5.

articles.headline: Seventeen Meetings, Seventeen Losses: The Giants Still Cannot Beat Philadelphia
articles.dek: New York lost 32-31 and 24-15 to the Eagles in Y95. Since Y88 the series stands at 17-0, and Washington's losing run reached 8.
body: Ty Lock's Giants came closer than anyone in Y95, and it was still not enough. In week 12 in New York they lost 32-31, the narrowest of the Eagles' 17 regular-season wins. In week 16 in Philadelphia the Eagles won 24-15. The series that began when Skura arrived in Y88 now stands at 17 meetings and 17 Philadelphia wins, with 572 points to New York's 374.

The Giants were otherwise a good team. They went 10-6-1, up from 9-8, though a week before the trip to Philadelphia they lost 20-13 at home to the 2-15 Cowboys. Lock, 39, threw for 3,488 yards and 31 touchdowns with 4 interceptions and has 627 touchdown passes in 330 games. Both of his rings came with Skura's Jets. Since Y88 the coach who won them with him has been the one obstacle he cannot clear.
Washington fared no better. The 12-5 Commanders, fifth in the power rankings with a rookie quarterback, lost 40-20 in Philadelphia and 36-14 at home, their 8th straight defeat by the Eagles.

articles.headline: Travon Swaim, 34, Is Defensive Player of the Year at Last
articles.dek: The Lions' defensive back made 232 tackles in 20 games and helped a 9-8 club reach the conference final.
body: Travon Swaim has spent a long career in Detroit without a ring, and Y95 brought him the next best thing. At 34 he made 232 tackles, second in the league to the 238 Isaiah Pinkney made for the Ravens, intercepted 3 passes and was named Defensive Player of the Year for the first time. He played all 20 of Detroit's games, playoffs included.

The Lions went 9-8 with a point differential of minus 56, then won twice in the playoffs before the Eagles beat them 30-16 in the conference final. Philadelphia had already beaten them 54-13 in week 5. Defensive lineman Landon Irwin, 22, led the league with 5 sacks.

The award moved Swaim's whole case. His Career Legacy climbed from 6,428 to 7,551 and his card's value more than doubled, from 2,459 to 5,983. He has 2,865 career tackles and 33 interceptions in 249 games. Every Defensive Player of the Year award on league cards has gone to a defensive back, and the newest one went to a player who waited longer than most.

articles.headline: Rookies Who Did Not Wait: Herbig, Howell, Rosas and Jarrett
articles.dek: Bryant Herbig threw 30 touchdown passes for the 12-5 Commanders, Tee Rosas tied for the league lead in interceptions, and Payton Jarrett won a ring.
body: Nineteen new players reached league cards in Y95, and several of them played like veterans. Bryant Herbig, 21, threw for 3,904 yards and 30 touchdowns with 3 interceptions for Washington, which went 12-5 and finished fifth in the power rankings. His tight end, fellow rookie Ulysees Howell, caught 107 passes, the fourth most in the league, though for only 551 yards, 5.1 a catch.
On defense Tee Rosas intercepted 5 passes for the 8-9 Steelers, tied with Lewis Pettis and Akayleb Samia for the league lead, and made 208 tackles. Teair Dye, 21, made 212 tackles for the Bengals.

The best rookie season came in Philadelphia. Payton Jarrett, 21, caught 81 passes for 1,450 yards and 15 touchdowns, second only to Calvin Wingo II in receiving yards, and won a ring in his first year. His card sells for 13. On that evidence, it will not stay there for long.

articles.headline: Two Interceptions From Hobbs: Brooker and Pettis Close In Together
articles.dek: Jamon Brooker and Lewis Pettis each have 41 career interceptions, 2 short of Damar Hobbs. Siran Spector moved to second on the rushing touchdown list.
body: Damar Hobbs's career interception record of 43 has two challengers, and they are tied. Jamon Brooker of the Packers picked off 1 pass in Y95 and Lewis Pettis of the Cowboys 5, and both finished at 41. Brooker is 32 and Pettis 34, so the clock is part of the race.

Siran Spector ran for 23 touchdowns for the Texans and reached 425, past Danny Diggs's 408 and Tim Wright's 417. Only Lane McCoy, with 458, has more, and Spector is 33 away. He also passed 20,000 career rushing yards.

One chase stopped. Kyron Atwell did not play a game in Y95 and stays at 3,059 tackles, 126 short of K'Lavon Settle's record 3,185. Another finally moved: Deshone Bello of the Jets got the sack he needed and drew level with Kalif Suh at 24.

articles.dek: Shootouts, a one-point thriller, a 39-year-old passer and three ties from around the league.
body: The Packers beat the Bears 64-53 in week 18, 117 points in all, the highest-scoring game of the season.
The Buccaneers beat the Packers 48-47 in week 7, 95 points in all and decided by 1.
Dustin Milton, 39, threw 40 touchdown passes and 2 interceptions for the 11-5-1 Patriots.
The Panthers allowed 653 points, the most in the league, and went 3-14.
The Browns scored 622 points, second only to the Eagles, and went 1-7 on the road.
Snoop Dotson made 102 tackles, the most by any linebacker, with 3 sacks and 2 forced fumbles, and won his 6th ring.
Three games ended in ties, among them the Bears and Giants at 27-27 in week 3.

didYouKnow.text: Ryland Maxwell's Career Legacy of 14,019 is now the highest on file, ahead of Sherman Brandson's 13,540.
Ryland Maxwell has 12 rings and 6 Super Bowl MVPs, both the most on file. Dorren Skura coached him to every ring, with the Jets, the Falcons and the Eagles.
Bones Crawford threw the most interceptions in the league in Y94, 20, and again in Y95, 10. He was named MVP in Y95 anyway.
The Cowboys lost all 8 of their home games in Y95, a year after ending the Eagles' 49-game winning streak.
The 15-2 Chiefs lost only to the 8-9 Cardinals and the 6-11 Raiders, two clubs with losing records.

Rookie tight end Ulysees Howell caught 107 passes for the Commanders and averaged 5.1 yards a catch.
Landon Irwin of the Lions led the league with 5 sacks in Y95. No other player had more than 3.
Payton Jarrett's 1,450 receiving yards as a rookie were the second most in the league, behind only his teammate Calvin Wingo II.
Y95 was the 13th unbeaten season of Dorren Skura's career. His Eagles had also gone 17-0 two seasons earlier, in Y93.

articles.headline: Six Straight: Eagles Beat the Bengals 40-26 in Super Bowl CLV
articles.dek: Philadelphia lost 4 regular-season games, its most under Dorren Skura, and still won a sixth straight title as Ryland Maxwell took a 7th Super Bowl MVP at 34.
body: The losses came, and the trophy came anyway. Dorren Skura's Eagles went 13-4 in Y96, the most regular-season defeats in his nine seasons in Philadelphia, after records of 17-0, 15-2 and 17-0 in the three years before. Then they beat the Bengals 40-26 in Super Bowl CLV, the 155th edition of the game, for the club's sixth straight championship.

The core never left the field. Ryland Maxwell, Bones Crawford, Akiem Brock and Calvin Wingo II each played all 21 of Philadelphia's games, playoffs included. Maxwell ran for 2,574 yards, the most in the league. Crawford threw 52 touchdown passes, also the most. Wingo led every receiver with 2,096 yards, and Brock made 62 blocks when no other lineman made more than 33.

Cincinnati arrived with the hottest runner in the league. Grover Calitro had scored 43 rushing touchdowns, the most in a season on league cards, and Alshon Lazard had turned his career back around. The Bengals put up 26 points in the final. Philadelphia scored 40.

It was not a farewell. Maxwell, 34, won his 13th ring and was named Super Bowl MVP for the 7th time. Brock, also 34, won his 8th ring, and Crawford won his 8th as well. Then the runner and the blocker who had been on the field for every title of the run both re-signed with Skura for one more year, and they open Y97 at 35. The question for the rest of the league is an old one: how to beat this team while its two constants are still on the field.

articles.headline: Mad Max at 34: 2,574 Yards, a 7th Super Bowl MVP and One More Year
articles.dek: Ryland Maxwell's Y96 was one of his best. He has 32,108 career rushing yards, 13 rings and the highest Career Legacy on file, and he re-signed for Y97.
body: Most great runners fade at 34. Ryland Maxwell sped up. He ran for 2,574 yards, 670 more than anyone else in the league, and scored 25 rushing touchdowns in 21 games. He stands at 32,108 career yards, the league record, 7,601 clear of Lane McCoy's 24,507.

The touchdown list is the one race he has not won yet. Maxwell's 421 rushing touchdowns top Skura's record board but rank third in the league, 4 behind Siran Spector's 425 and 37 behind McCoy's 458. Everything else is already his: 125 career touchdown catches, 13 rings and 7 Super Bowl MVPs, the last two both the most on file.

His Career Legacy stands at 14,903, the highest on file, and the Hall of Fame watch scores him at 100, the maximum, far above the bar of 65. The Hall will have to wait. Skura re-signed him in Y96, and he opens Y97 at 35, still an Eagle. Every one of his rings came with Dorren Skura: 2 with the Jets, 5 with the Falcons and 6 with the Eagles. One ordinary season would carry him past Spector, and few backs have ever been given the chance to try at 35.

articles.headline: Akiem Brock Has 8 Rings, a Hall of Fame Case and One More Year to Play
articles.dek: The league's best blocker made 62 blocks in Y96 at 34, and he and Ryland Maxwell are both back for another run.
body: No lineman on league cards came near Akiem Brock in Y96, and none had for years. He made 62 blocks in 21 games, 29 more than JD Pircher of the Bengals or Caleb Linsley of the Giants, and passed 500 for his career on the way to 538 in 181 games.

He spent his whole card career in Philadelphia, and the rings followed: 8 of them, every one with Dorren Skura. In nine seasons together, Skura's Eagles won the title eight times. Y90 was the one that got away.

The Hall of Fame watch scores him at 79, the best standing among offensive linemen and well clear of the bar of 65; Maxwell's is 100, the maximum. His Career Legacy stands at 11,394 and his card at 29,312. He was 34 in Y96, the same age as Maxwell, and both re-signed with Skura to play Y97 at 35. Linemen rarely get the headlines in a dynasty built on a record-setting runner and a quarterback who threw 52 touchdown passes in Y96. When the vote does come, it will say what the box scores never could: the runner and the quarterback had help.

articles.headline: Leglue's MVP at 36 Is a Verdict on Crawford's 17 Interceptions
articles.dek: Bones Crawford threw 52 touchdown passes, 11 more than anyone, and led the league in interceptions for a third straight season. The award went to Detroit.
body: Margus Leglue has spent his whole card career in Detroit, and at 36 he finally won the league's top award. He threw for 3,803 yards and 41 touchdowns with 1 interception in 19 games and was named Most Valuable Player for the first time. His overall rose from 78 to 84 and his card from 237 to 874.

The case against Bones Crawford made itself. He threw 52 touchdown passes, the most in the league, and 17 interceptions, when no other quarterback threw more than 6. It was the third season in a row he led the league in interceptions, after 20 in Y94 and 10 in Y95, and this time the voters held it against him. His MVP count stays at 5.

The market took the other side. Crawford's card value rose 124.4% to 19,210, and he collected his 8th ring. Leglue has the trophy; Crawford has the jewellery and the price tag. One of them was the better quarterback in Y96, and the argument will outlast both careers.

articles.headline: Calitro's 43 Touchdowns Break the Season Mark and Carry Cincinnati to the Final
articles.dek: Grover Calitro passed Siran Spector's 42 for the most rushing touchdowns in a season on file, and Alshon Lazard found his game again. The Bengals fell 40-26 in Super Bowl CLV.
body: Two seasons ago Cincinnati went 6-11 and its young quarterback was a cautionary tale. In Y96 the Bengals were the last club standing between the Eagles and a sixth straight title, and they lost Super Bowl CLV 40-26.

Grover Calitro was the reason they got there. He ran for 1,904 yards, second only to Ryland Maxwell, and scored 43 rushing touchdowns, the most in a single season on league cards, one more than Siran Spector's 42 for Houston in Y89. Nobody else in the league scored more than 30. He played all 21 games.

Alshon Lazard threw 39 touchdown passes as a rookie in Y93 and fell to 18 a year later. In Y96 he found the middle: 3,749 yards, 33 touchdowns and 2 interceptions. Teair Dye, in his second season, made 225 tackles.

The critics will point to what Calitro did not win. The Offensive Player of the Year award went to Alton Yeldon of the Seahawks, who ran for 1,558 yards and 27 touchdowns. A record season and no trophy: Cincinnati will take the trip to the final instead.

articles.headline: Brooker Draws Level With Hobbs at 43, and Swaim Climbs to Third on the Tackle List
articles.dek: Jamon Brooker tied the career interception record, Lewis Pettis was shut out, and Ryland Maxwell sits 4 rushing touchdowns short of second place.
body: A year ago Jamon Brooker and Lewis Pettis were tied at 41 interceptions, 2 short of Damar Hobbs. Brooker got both in Y96. He picked off 2 passes for the Packers and now shares the career record of 43 with Hobbs. At 33, he needs one more to own it.
Pettis played all 17 of the Cowboys' games and did not intercept a pass. He stays at 41, though his overall still rose from 95 to 97.

Travon Swaim made 199 tackles for the Lions and reached 3,064, passing Kyron Atwell's 3,059 for third on the career list. Only K'Lavon Settle, at 3,185, and Terron Stidham, at 3,132, have more, and Swaim is 121 from the record.

Angelo Moton of the Packers scored 30 rushing touchdowns and passed 350 for his career. And the chase still open: Maxwell is at 421, 4 short of Spector's 425 for second on that list, and he is back for Y97.

articles.headline: Ty Lock's Long Goodbye, and the Rookie Who Took His Place
articles.dek: The Giants' quarterback since Y83 is retired after 330 games and 627 touchdown passes. Yurik Okudah threw 34 in his first season.
body: Ty Lock's retirement is now on the record, and his last snaps came in Y95, when he was 39. He played 330 games, threw for 68,237 yards and 627 touchdowns with 137 interceptions, and won 2 MVP awards. Both of his rings came early, with Dorren Skura's Jets, before a multi-team trade sent him to New York ahead of Y83.
New York was his home for thirteen seasons and never gave him a ring. From Y88 on, the obstacle was his old coach: by the end of Y95 the Giants had met Skura's Eagles 17 times and lost all 17.

His successor arrived ready. Yurik Okudah, a rookie, threw for 3,610 yards and 34 touchdowns with 2 interceptions in 19 games. His card sells for 23, the price of an unknown, but the market's skill grade already reads A+. Lock spent a career chasing Philadelphia. Okudah has time to start his own chase.

articles.headline: Rashawn Elder Catches 122 Passes, and the Class of Y95 Keeps Coming
articles.dek: A rookie tight end led the league in catches, Mario Lamb scored 28 times for the Chiefs, and Payton Jarrett has 2 rings in 2 seasons.
body: Twenty-one new players reached league cards in Y96. The busiest was Rashawn Elder of the Colts, a tight end who caught 122 passes, the most in the league, though for only 675 yards, 5.5 a catch. Mario Lamb ran for 1,463 yards and 28 touchdowns for the Chiefs, Damiere Norton threw 28 touchdown passes for the Patriots, and Rico Gee threw 25 with 1 interception for the Cowboys.

Last year's class did not slow down. Bryant Herbig threw 30 touchdown passes for the Commanders for the second straight season, Teair Dye made 225 tackles for the Bengals, and tight end Ulysees Howell caught 81 passes.

Payton Jarrett had the best of it again: 74 catches, 1,419 yards and 16 touchdowns, second in the league in receiving yards behind Calvin Wingo II for the second year running, and a 2nd ring in his 2nd season. His overall rose from 67 to 72 and his card from 13 to 37. It is still a bargain.

articles.dek: A second Defensive Player of the Year award, a tight end's leap and a linebacker who led the league in sacks.
body: Abraham Jack of the Bills was Defensive Player of the Year for the 2nd time, with 237 tackles, tied with A.T. Hoyer of the Raiders for the most.
Alton Yeldon of the Seahawks was Offensive Player of the Year for the first time.
Jacob Proise's overall jumped from 84 to 93 and his card from 1,109 to 5,527 after 786 yards and 14 touchdown catches.
Snoop Dotson led the league with 4 sacks and 2 forced fumbles, added 5 interceptions and won his 7th ring.
Lenny Baun of the Dolphins intercepted 6 passes, the most in the league.
Calvin Wingo II caught 104 passes for 2,096 yards and 18 touchdowns, the most receiving yards in the league for a second straight season.
Koa Zuber, "Uber Feasts", won his 7th ring with 131 tackles and 2 interceptions.
